prompt_en: An environmental editorial photograph inside a restored indoor ferry terminal at autumn dusk. A fictional adult woman is seated on the broad central stone bench; use the supplied image solely for visible face and hair appearance, with a dark chin-length bob, wispy parted bangs, dark eyes and the visible facial contours. She has paused midway through folding a creased paper route map across her lap and looks toward the camera with a quietly attentive expression. Her hips rest fully on the bench, her left foot rests on the floor, and her right foot rests on a low stone step. Her separated knees support her forearms, with the right elbow higher than the left; her head is the upper apex and the two outward elbows form the lower corners of a clear seated triangle. Her shoulders tilt gently and her head leans slightly toward the lower shoulder, creating an asymmetrical pose. The camera faces the exact central doorway: matching arched passages and paired wall lamps mirror each other on both sides, with upright columns and level floor seams. A wicker basket of dried hydrangeas sits beside the bench. Behind the bench, two travelers cross laterally through the paired passages as translucent directional motion trails, while her eyes, facial contours, hands and folded map remain crisp and stationary. The bench and architecture are sharply resolved too. Warm light from the two wall lamps meets cool overcast entrance light, with a brief soft frontal flash making the face readable during the slow exposure. Frame from her head through both feet, large enough to read both eyes, retaining the bench supports and both symmetrical passageways. A tripod-mounted 50mm lens holds the frontal view. Clean digital detail preserves skin pores, paper fibers and dry petal edges. Between the lamp-lit arches, the face retains focal priority within the paired architecture. On the bench, the primary subject keeps a readable stationary support and pose; the requested facial region remains comparatively resolved. Behind her, a separate moving peripheral element leaves a directional exposure trail, and the trail and sharp subject occupy coherently related scene planes.
